Subject: Model fit recap + prompt set collection for Acme search assistant

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move into an evaluation phase: 

Summary from discovery
- Goal: Replace current keyword search with an LLM-powered contextual search assistant for product docs and support tickets.
- Key constraints: 95th pct latency target < 400ms for short queries, redaction of PII before any tokens hit the model, and retention policy of 30 days.
- Primary persona: internal support agents + end users on web search widget.

Recommended model candidates (tradeoffs)
- Redwood-1.6-instruct (low-latency, good for short Q&A / retrieval-augmented generation)
- Redwood-Chat-4x (balanced: better multi-turn/context handling, modest latency)
- Llama-2-70b-chat (high-quality/long-context; higher cost and infra needs)

Benchmarks & eval resources
- Short benchmark summary: https://redwood.dev/benchmarks/acme-search (will seed with your query profile)
- Full benchmark deck (internal): redwood_benchmark_report_q1.pdf (attached)
- Prompt/template to collect from your team: acme_prompt_template.txt (attached)

Ask: can you share 3 buckets of example prompts by next Thursday (2026-03-18)?
1) Typical queries (top ~200 by volume)
2) Edge/ambiguous queries (where retrieval may fail)
3) PII examples that you absolutely must redact (emails, full names+SSNs, order numbers, etc.)
Format: CSV or plaintext with one prompt per line; if you can include expected/desired assistant responses that helps us build the eval. See the attached template.

Redaction note: please do not send raw PII to the evaluation workspace — if you need to show structure, replace sensitive fields with placeholders (e.g., <EMAIL_REDACTED>, <SSN_REDACTED>). We can run a small set of synthetic or redacted examples with real-like distribution for quality checks.

Next steps
- You: send the prompt buckets + a point of contact on engineering/legal for redaction questions (cc'd legal@acme-corp.com if applicable).
- Us: we will spin up an eval workspace, run baseline on Redwood-Chat-4x and Redwood-1.6-instruct, and share back precision/latency/quality tradeoff notes.

If this looks right I’ll follow up with an invite to a short alignment call with our eval engineer (Dev) to agree on format and redaction regex.

Thanks — looking forward to the sample prompts.

Best,

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Sarah. Short answers and an engineering suggestion below.

Redaction guidance (recommended)
- Preferred: client-side redaction before requests reach our routers. Replace PII with clear placeholders (e.g., <EMAIL_REDACTED>) so we can preserve tokenization/context and avoid accidental leakage.
- If you need uniqueness to help with troubleshooting, hash values with a consistent salt before sending (server-side) — that keeps uniqueness without exposing the original.
- Avoid sending raw SSNs/emails even in test workspace; use synthetic/scrubbed examples where possible.

Technical tradeoffs
- Placeholder approach: keeps model context readable and reproducible for evals; easiest to interpret during human review.
- Hash/pseudonym approach: preserves per-entity uniqueness which can help ranking/retrieval quality tests, but makes human review harder. Choose only if necessary.

Engineering next steps
- Please share the three buckets by 2026-03-18 (we can accept partial deliveries).
- We will provision an eval workspace and seed it with your retrieval index (if you provide a small export or sample documents) and run baseline tests on Redwood-Chat-4x and Redwood-1.6-instruct.
- Dev & Dylan: can you prepare a small eval harness (50 synthetic + 50 redacted real prompts) and baseline runs by Mon 2026-03-16? I’ll drop the inputs once Sarah sends them.

If legal has specific wording needed in our eval NDA, loop them into the HubSpot record and I’ll escalate with our contracts team.

Thanks again — we should have a short sync after you send the prompts.

Best,
Marissa
